hook: When Dracula came out in 1897, Transylvania wasn't in Romania.
twist: It was part of the Kingdom of Hungary inside Austria-Hungary; it joined Romania only in 1918-1920. Bram Stoker never went there, the real Vlad the Impaler ruled Wallachia (south of the mountains), and 'Dracula's Castle' at Bran was picked for tourists decades later. Dracula never moved: the border did.
angle: Why is Dracula's homeland in Romania? A Halloween-week border story told on a real map of the Carpathians: the 1897 border, the 1918 union and the 1920 treaty, with the Vlad and Bran myths as payoffs.
why_now: Halloween (31 October) is four days after the 27 October slot. risks: Trianon is a live grievance in Hungary and a national holiday story in Romania: state the dates neutrally, no jokes about the transfer, mention that the union was proclaimed by Transylvania's Romanian delegates and confirmed by treaty.
